div.div:
System bus: AXI crossbar (axi_xbar)
Replaced the former soc_axi_arbiter + soc_axi_demux (in place today). Per-target arbitration; multiple outstanding requests can be in flight to different targets concurrently.
In the end state the xbar exposes only ~2 slave targets: the peripheral subsystem (one APB bus) and an optional RAM-fallback path (mostly used by debug SBA).

div.div:
Why this layered shape?
Memory subsystem (soc_mem_ss): per-bank arbitration. Memory-heavy initiators (CPU instr/data, DMA, accelerators) get dedicated init ports so bank parallelism actually pays off - the bus fabric does not gate memory bandwidth.
System bus (axi_xbar): per-target AXI arbitration. In the end state the xbar exposes only ~2 slave targets: the peripheral subsystem and an optional RAM-fallback path. The xbar is small because most traffic does not need it.
Peripheral subsystem (APB bus): a single APB peripheral bus behind one soc_axi_to_apb bridge. UART, CLINT (wrapped), DM regs (wrapped), accelerator CSR windows, and future SPI/I2C/GPIO/timers all fan out from one APB demux. Adding a new peripheral is "add to the APB subsystem", not "reconfigure the xbar".
What grows linearly: arbiters. M arbiters in the xbar for M targets (only a handful in the end state); B arbiters in soc_mem_ss for B banks; the APB subsystem needs no arbitration (peripherals are slaves, they do not initiate). Wires fan out N x B inside soc_mem_ss but synthesis handles that cleanly at this scale.
